topic: UN High Seas Treaty Enters Into Force

subtopics.title: BBNJ Agreement: scope and objectives
subtopics.summary: The UN High Seas Treaty, also called the BBNJ Agreement, is a legally binding treaty for ocean spaces beyond national jurisdiction. It was negotiated under a UN-led intergovernmental conference and aims to safeguard biodiversity in these areas. It contributes to the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, which targets 30% protection of land and sea by 2030.
facts: Also called UN High Seas Treaty; adopted in 2023.
Legally binding international treaty governing ocean spaces beyond national jurisdiction.
Covers the high seas and the International Seabed Area.
These areas are global commons, open to all states for navigation, overflight, submarine cables and pipelines.
Third implementing agreement under UNCLOS, alongside the 1994 Part XI Agreement and the 1995 UN Fish Stocks Agreement.
Core objective: safeguard biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction.
Contributes to the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.
Four pillars: Marine Genetic Resources, Area-Based Management Tools, Environmental Impact Assessments, Capacity Building and Technology Transfer.
Conference of the Parties (COP) is the decision-making body.
Ratified by 83 countries; India has signed, ratification pending.

subtopics.title: UNCLOS and maritime zones
subtopics.summary: The 1982 UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) sets the legal framework for all activities in the oceans and seas and is called the constitution for the oceans. It divides ocean space into zones with different levels of state control, from full sovereignty in the territorial sea to free navigation on the high seas. It also created three international institutions.
facts: UNCLOS (1982) is also called the constitution for the oceans.
It has 168 parties and sets out the legal framework for all activities in the oceans and seas.
The Convention created three new institutions at the international level.
International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea: independent judicial body for disputes on interpretation or application of the Convention.
International Seabed Authority: ensures protection of the marine environment from harmful effects of deep-seabed activities.
Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf: facilitates establishing outer limits of the continental shelf beyond 200 NM from baselines.
Territorial sea: the state has full sovereignty.
Exclusive Economic Zone: extends to 200 NM; the state has the right to exploit all economic resources.
High seas: free for navigation by vessels of all nations.
1 NM (nautical mile) = 1.852 km.

subtopics.title: Fisheries sector in India and its schemes
subtopics.summary: India's fisheries sector contributes 7.43% to agriculture gross value added, the highest among agriculture and allied sectors. India ranks high globally as a producer, aquaculture producer and exporter. Government schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana aim to modernise the sector and support fish farmers and micro and small enterprises.
facts: Total fish output (2024-25): 197.75 lakh tonnes.
Fisheries contribute 7.43% to agriculture GVA, the highest among agriculture and allied sectors.
India is the 2nd largest producer (8% of world production) and 2nd largest aquaculture producer.
India is the 4th largest exporter; the United States is the largest importer of Indian seafood.
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana was introduced in 2020 under the Atma Nirbhar Bharat Package.
Matsya Sampada investment: Rs 20,050 crore.
National Fisheries Development Board, established 2006, works under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying.
PM Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana: sub-scheme for fisheries micro and small enterprises, investment Rs 6,000 crore.
Implementation period of the Sah-Yojana: 2023-24 to 2026-27.
India's first riverine dolphin estimation counted 6,327 dolphins across 28 rivers in 8 states.

subtopics.title: WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
subtopics.summary: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies was adopted at the 12th Ministerial Conference in 2022 and entered into force in September 2025. It aims to set binding rules to curb harmful fisheries subsidies, especially those linked to illegal fishing. India did not join the agreement, citing the need to protect small fishers, livelihoods and food security.
facts: Adopted at the 12th Ministerial Conference, 2022.
Entered into force in September 2025, after approval by two-thirds of members.
Objective: establish binding rules to curb harmful fisheries subsidies.
Prohibited: subsidies linked to Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated (IUU) fishing.
Prohibited: subsidies for fishing on overfished stocks.
Prohibited: support for fishing in unregulated high seas.
Members must submit fisheries-related data.
Supports SDG 14: conserve and sustainably use oceans, seas and marine resources.
India did not join, citing the need to protect small fishers, livelihoods and food security.
WTO Fish Fund provides aid to developing and LDC members for implementation.

quizzes.passage: India's fisheries sector is part of the agriculture and allied sectors, and it makes a notable contribution to agricultural output. The sector covers both capture fisheries and aquaculture, and India also exports seafood to buyers abroad. The government has launched several schemes to strengthen the sector. The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana was introduced as part of the Atma Nirbhar Bharat Package, with the aim of bringing a Blue Revolution through the sustainable and responsible development of fisheries. Its focus areas include modernising fisheries infrastructure, promoting sustainable aquaculture practices, improving post-harvest management, and enhancing the livelihoods of fishers and fish farmers. A sub-scheme under it, the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana, supports micro and small enterprises operating in the sector and aims to formalise the sector under a national digital platform. The sector is also supported by integrated aqua parks, with parks planned in several states, and by a plan to develop climate resilient coastal fishermen villages. The scheme also aims to enhance fish production and productivity in India, to double farmers' income, and to coordinate fishery development in an integrated and holistic manner. A Fisheries Infrastructure Development Fund also envisages the creation of fisheries infrastructure in both marine and inland fisheries.

quizzes.passage: India's fisheries sector covers both capture fisheries and aquaculture, and it is supported by a range of government schemes. The National Fisheries Development Board is the nodal agency for the sector and works under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. Its headquarters are in Hyderabad, Telangana. Fisheries is a State subject in India. The Board is involved in the Matsya Setu App, which was launched together with ICAR's Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture in Bhubaneswar to offer online training modules for fish farmers and stakeholders. The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, introduced as part of the Atma Nirbhar Bharat Package, aims to modernise fisheries infrastructure and support sustainable aquaculture practices. Under it, a sub-scheme for micro and small enterprises in the sector seeks to formalise the sector under a national digital platform. The sector also includes five integrated aqua parks in several states and a plan to develop climate resilient coastal fishermen villages. A Fisheries Infrastructure Development Fund envisages infrastructure in both marine and inland fisheries, with lending through NABARD, the National Cooperative Development Corporation and scheduled banks. India's first riverine dolphin estimation was carried out to assess the population and conservation needs of river dolphins, and it recorded the highest population in Uttar Pradesh.

quizzes.passage: The UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, also called the constitution for the oceans, sets out the legal framework within which all activities in the oceans and seas must be carried out. The UN High Seas Treaty, or BBNJ Agreement, is a legally binding international treaty governing ocean spaces beyond national jurisdiction. The high seas and the international seabed area are considered global commons, open to all states for activities such as navigation, overflight and laying of submarine cables and pipelines. The 1994 Agreement on Part XI deals with deep seabed mining, and the 1995 UN Fish Stocks Agreement is another implementing agreement under the Convention. The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies was adopted at the 12th Ministerial Conference in 2022. Its objective is to establish binding rules that curb harmful fisheries subsidies. The agreement entered into force in September 2025, after two-thirds of members had approved it. It supports Sustainable Development Goal 14, which aims to conserve and sustainably use oceans, seas and marine resources. The WTO Fish Fund provides aid to developing and least developed country members for implementing the agreement. The International Seabed Authority has the mandate to ensure the effective protection of the marine environment from harmful effects that may arise from deep-seabed related activities.

The UN High Seas Treaty, or BBNJ Agreement, is a legally binding international treaty governing ocean spaces beyond national jurisdiction. Its core objective is to safeguard biodiversity in high seas areas beyond national jurisdiction. The high seas and the international seabed area are considered global commons, open to all states for activities such as navigation, overflight and laying of submarine cables and pipelines. The International Seabed Authority works to protect the marine environment from harmful effects of deep-seabed related activities. The Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf helps implement the Convention on the outer limits of the continental shelf.
